decisions.why: The benedícere (man → God) row keeps the Latin's two cases at no cost: accusative *bendizei o Senhor* (133), dative *bendizei ao Senhor*, and names 102:20–22 among the datives. Every Ps 102 place is the dative. The Greek has the accusative everywhere (εὐλόγει … τὸν κύριον), so by D15's test the Latin's case is not a difference of sense; but the row is working and Portuguese carries the dative with no loss, and in 102:1 the *ao* is what lets the verbless second colon (*ao seu santo nome*) be heard as a second 'bless'. Ps 95:2 turned a dative noun object direct on the stylist's word ('dated'); the row itself says it may want revisiting. Ruled for the row; the direct object is one touch away.

options.label: ao Senhor
options.note: draft — the row's dative; parallel to *ao seu santo nome* in 102:1

options.label: o Senhor
options.note: direct object, as 133 and as MS1932 here (*Bendize, ó minha alma, o Senhor*); with it 102:1b should become *o seu santo nome* (decision omnia)

decisions.why: The soul is addressed, singular, so *tu* (*Bendize*). The vocative is marked with *ó* so that *minha alma* is not heard as the subject of a third person *bendize* ('my soul blesses'); MS1932 has *ó minha alma* in all three places. The refrain 41:6 / 42:5 has no *ó* (*Por que estás triste, minha alma?*), but there the verb is a question in the second person and cannot be misheard.

decisions.latin: et ómnia, quæ intra me sunt, nómini sancto ejus
decisions.why: The Latin gaps the verb: *ómnia quæ intra me sunt* is a second addressee of *Bénedic*, and *nómini sancto ejus* its dative. MS1932 supplies *(bendigam)* in parentheses, a gloss. Kept verbless: the dative *ao* in both colons makes the parallel audible (bless the Lord … all within me, his holy name). *dentro de mim* keeps *intra*; *há* is the plain verb for *sunt* here.

decisions.latin: et noli oblivísci omnes retributiónes ejus
decisions.why: *retribútio → retribuição* (the row: 'neutral on purpose — it is a good thing in 102:2'). *noli oblivísci omnes* is 'forget none of': Portuguese *não esqueças todas* would say 'do not forget all of them (some you may)', a scope the Latin does not have. *nenhuma das* is grammar (the negation's scope), under D2. MS1932 and DRB both render the sense (*nenhum dos seus benefícios*; 'all he hath done for thee').

decisions.why: **Flagged for Gustavo: this verse is named in the propitiári row as awaiting his ruling on the family.** The row's current state: where the object is a sin, *ser clemente com* (78:9 *sede clemente com os nossos pecados*; 77:38 *será clemente com os pecados deles*), because *ser propício a* was heard by two blind readers (24:11, 64:4) as God favouring the sin, and *propício* was listed as unknown. The row proposes for this verse, word for word, *que é clemente com todas as tuas iniquidades*; applied. *perdoar* stays dimíttere's; *misericórdia* has its own word in 102:4. The Greek is εὐιλατεύοντα, 'being gracious towards'.

decisions.why: Five relative clauses hang on *Dómino … ejus* of 102:2, three of them opening a verse. Kept as bare *Que … que …*, the Latin's build and its anaphora: the sentence runs on from 102:2 as the Latin does. The risk is that a verse-initial *Que* is heard as a question; the colons end in plain nouns and no question follows, so the risk was judged small — the ambiguity reader is the test. MS1932 makes each verse a cleft main clause (*É ele que perdoa …*), which reads cleanly but collides with *é clemente* (*É ele que é clemente*).

options.label: É ele que
options.note: MS1932's cleft; with *é clemente* it doubles the *é*

decisions.why: *intéritus → destruição* (row, 9:16a, 34:7). DRB 'destruction'. MS1932 *da morte* interprets. The Greek φθορά is 'corruption', which the Latin does not say.

decisions.latin: Qui replet in bonis desidérium tuum
decisions.why: *replére → encher* (row, passive so far; kept apart from *satiáre / saturáre → saciar*). Active here, *encher de bens*. *bens* can be heard as possessions (Ps 4's ambiguity reader); after *encher de* it is the phrase of good things (the Magnificat's *bonis* is commonly *encheu de bens* in Brazil — from memory, not verified). MS1932 *sacia* is satiáre's verb.

The subject comes last in the Latin, and *juventude* is a good paroxytone close; *águia* at the end would put the final stress three syllables back. The verb moved after the comparison to avoid mesóclise (*renovar-se-á*, MS1932's order) — order only. v2: the stylist and the ambiguity reader both stumbled on *como a da águia* at the head (the pronoun comes before its noun); the plain order taken.

decisions.why: *judícium → juízo* (D15). *fáciens* governs both nouns; the second colon keeps the Latin's gapping, so the ear does not meet the colloquial *fazer juízo* ('come to one's senses', 118:121's stylist). MS1932 *faz justiça* is the Portuguese idiom, but *justiça* is justítia's, and justítia is in this psalm (102:17b). *para todos* for the dative of advantage.

'Those who suffer wrong' (ἀδικουμένοις). *injúria* in Brazil is chiefly an insult; MS1932 *agravos* is correct but formal. *injustiça* is the plain word and is heard rightly; it shares a word with injustítia (a different Latin noun, the same Greek root), which never stands in this verse.

The pair is the row's *compassivo e misericordioso* (85:15). The Latin sets the adjectives first. The plain order (*O Senhor é compassivo e misericordioso*) would end the mediant on *misericordioso* and the verse on *misericordioso* too — a rhyme at mediant and final the Latin does not have (its mediant is *Dóminus*). The Latin's order keeps *o Senhor* at the mediant, as the Latin does, and the second *misericordioso* at the end, where the Latin puts its second *miséricors*. 144:8 has the same line and should copy it.

decisions.latin: Non in perpétuum irascétur: * neque in ætérnum comminábitur
decisions.why: Two phrases in one verse: *in perpétuum* (εἰς τέλος — the Greek of *in finem*) and *in ætérnum* (εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα → *para sempre*, D23). D27 keeps εἰς τέλος apart from *in ætérnum*, and merged, the verse would say *para sempre* twice where the Latin varies. *perpetuamente* is the cognate, plain, and MS1932's word (*perpètuamente*). *in perpétuum* occurs nowhere else in the Gallican psalter (grep; only in canticles). *até o fim* would fail in the negative as 9:19 did.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: D27's perpetuity reading of εἰς τέλος; the verse then repeats *para sempre*

options.label: para sempre … eternamente
options.note: the stylist's swap (*Não estará irado para sempre: * nem ameaçará eternamente*); needs the second colon changed too and breaks D23 (*in ætérnum → para sempre*, *eternamente* its refused option)

decisions.why: The Latinist (v1, minor) asks the simple future *se irará* (the act, not a state), parallel to *ameaçará*. Held for the irásci row: 79:5 and 84:6 made the future a copula + participle because *vos irareis* is a knot of r's, and *se irará perpetuamente* is the same knot. The state reading is inside the verse's sense (not angry for ever).

ἐκραταίωσεν. No row. κραταιόω is the Greek of *confortétur* in 26:14 (*que o teu coração se fortaleça*), so by D15's test the verb is *fortalecer*. MS1932 *firmou* would collide with *firmáre / confirmáre* (32:6, 118:38).

decisions.why: *longe fecit* keeps the adverb (the perto / longe row: *pôr longe*); *tão* supplies the correlative Portuguese needs for *Quantum* (grammar). MS1932 *tanto ele afastou* loses *longe*.

decisions.why: *figméntum* (πλάσμα) is the thing formed — the potter's work; the next verse says what it is made of (*pulvis*). No plain Portuguese noun: *feitura* is factúra's (91:5), *formação* is heard as schooling, *massa* adds. The noun is said as a clause, as D16 did with *elóquium*: *de que somos formados* is MS1932's own wording, and with a clause for object *cognóscere* takes *saber* (the row, 13:4). *cognóvit* is the perfect of knowing, present in sense (DRB 'knoweth'; D44 *conheço*). *ipse → ele mesmo*, as 67:36 and 43:5.

decisions.latin: homo, sicut fænum dies ejus, tamquam flos agri sic efflorébit
decisions.why: *homo* hangs at the head and is the subject of *efflorébit*. Kept as a hanging subject so that *florescerá* is still the man's; MS1932 and DRB make it *os dias do homem*, after which *florescerá* could belong to the days. The Latin order of the comparison (*sicut fænum dies ejus*) is kept so that the two *como* answer each other. *fænum → erva*: the fænum row splits by what the grass does; here it stands beside the flower of the field and the next verse is a wind passing over it — living grass, not hay (the row: *erva* is the candidate if one word is wanted). v2: the stylist's order taken for the comparison; the hanging *o homem* stays.

decisions.why: *spíritus* (πνεῦμα) is wind and breath at once: a wind passing over the flower, or the life-breath passing out of the man. Portuguese *espírito* has lost 'wind' and would be heard as the soul or the Holy Spirit; *vento* keeps only the wind (MS1932 *sopro de vento*). *sopro* is both breath and gust, so it keeps the Latin's openness. *e não subsistirá* keeps the Latin's open subject (the man or the flower).

options.label: o espírito
options.note: the cognate, DRB 'the spirit'; heard as the soul

options.label: um vento
options.note: MS1932's reading (*um sopro de vento*); closes the ambiguity

decisions.latin: Et justítia illíus in fílios filiórum
decisions.why: *in* + accusative, 'unto, towards' (ἐπὶ υἱοὺς υἱῶν). *para* is the plain preposition and is echoed by *para os que* (the dative *his*), as the two members are one extent. *sobre* would echo *super timéntes* of 102:17 but the Latin changes preposition; *até* makes it a limit.
*serváre* (a law, a covenant) → *observar* (open row; 102:17 named among its five places); *custodíre* keeps *guardar*. *testaméntum → aliança* (row). MS1932 *guardam*, the idiom, is the option.

options.label: guardam
options.note: MS1932; custodíre's verb; the stylist (v1) asked it as plainer — refused for the row (custodíre keeps *guardar*); the ambiguity reader heard *observam* as keep

decisions.latin: ad faciéndum ea · faciéntes verbum illíus · qui fácitis voluntátem ejus
decisions.why: One Latin verb three times in four verses. *fazer* cannot take *palavra* or *mandamentos* in Portuguese; *cumprir* can (the row fácere (justificatiónes) → *cumprir*). *fácere voluntátem* is *fazer a vontade* in 39:9 (*que eu faça a vossa vontade*), the Our Father's verb, so 102:21 keeps it; the repetition is kept in two of three. The option makes all three *cumprir* and breaks 39:9's formula.

options.label: cumprir ×3
options.note: the repetition whole; breaks 39:9's *fazer a vontade*

options.label: MS1932
options.note: MS1932 (*para os observar*, *executores da sua palavra*); *observar* is serváre's (102:17b)

decisions.why: *ómnibus* can be masculine or neuter (all men, all things); the Greek πάντων is as open. *sobre todos* leans to persons but does not exclude all things; *sobre tudo* closes it the other way. MS1932 *sobre todos*.

δυνατοὶ ἰσχύι. The virtus row: *poder* for God's, *vigor* for a creature's own strength where the Greek is ἰσχύς (21:16, 37:11, 70:9). *poderosos em poder* would stutter; *força* is fortitúdo's. DRB 'mighty in strength'. v2: the stylist's *força* taken as a local departure; *vigor* stays the option.

options.label: força
options.note: v2 — the stylist's (and DRB 'mighty in strength'): *poderosos em vigor* heard as tautological and stiff. A local departure from the virtus row's *vigor*: the angels' ἰσχύς; fortitúdo does not occur in this psalm

options.label: vigor
options.note: draft 1 — the virtus row's proposal for ἰσχύς; the stylist heard *poderosos em vigor* as a tautology

decisions.latin: faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum ejus
decisions.why: D15 names this verse: *verbum* and *sermo* side by side, one Greek word (and here the Greek repeats it: τὸν λόγον … τῶν λόγων), so *palavra … palavras* as D15 rules; the verse decides locally. 55:11 kept the Latin's variation with *fala*; that is the option. MS1932 and DRB *ordens / orders* interpret. v2: the stylist heard *palavra … palavras* as a jingle at the cadence and asked *do seu falar*; refused for D15 (the Greek has the same repetition), kept as an option.

options.label: do seu falar
options.note: the stylist (v1): the echo *palavra … palavras* lands on the final cadence. Refused: the Greek repeats λόγος, D15 merges verbum and sermo; *falar* as a noun is a third shape

decisions.why: πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ, the heavenly powers. D43 renders *Dóminus virtútum* 'o Senhor dos poderes', the same plural; kept, so the Latin's one word stays one. DRB 'hosts', MS1932 'milícia' (the Hebrew's *ṣәbā'āyw*).

options.label: virtudes
options.note: the cognate (83:8's choice); heard as moral virtues

choices.102:1: The soul is a singular addressee: *tu* (*Bendize*). *intra me → dentro de mim*.
choices.102:3: *sanáre → curar* (row); *infirmitátes → enfermidades* (the infírmus row names this verse). **propitiári: flagged for Gustavo** (see decision).
choices.102:4: *redímere → resgatar* (row). *coronáre → coroar* (row) with *de*, as 8:6 *de glória e de honra o coroastes*. *miseratiónes → compaixões* (row; side by side with *misericórdia* as 24:6, 50:3).
choices.102:5: *juvéntus → juventude* (42:4). The verse ends with a colon, as the Latin, running into 102:6.
choices.102:6: *Fáciens* made a finite verb (grammar); *misericórdias* plural as the Latin (ἐλεημοσύνας; MS1932 *faz misericórdias*).
choices.102:7: *Notas fecit → Fez conhecer* (the notum fácere row: 15:11, 76:15, 97:2). No *e* between the colons, as the Latin (MS1932 adds one). *Móyses → Moisés* (row). *voluntátes* plural kept (*vontades*, MS1932).
choices.102:8: 144:8 has the same Latin and should copy this verse. *multum miséricors → muito misericordioso*, not 85:15's *de muita misericórdia* (a different Latin, as the multæ misericórdiæ row warns).
choices.102:9: *irascétur → estará irado*, the copula future of 79:5 / 84:6 (*se irará* is a knot of r's). *comminári → ameaçar*.
choices.102:10: *fácere + dative → tratar* (the fácere cum row: *Tratai o vosso servo*); MS1932 *Não nos tratou*. *retríbuit → retribuiu* (17:21).
choices.102:11: *secúndum altitúdinem → segundo a altura* (the altitúdo row names this verse: the concrete word). *a terra* ('from the earth') → *acima da terra*, the height measured upward. *super timéntes se → sobre os que o temem*.
choices.102:12: *ortus / occidens → oriente / ocidente* (MS1932): *ortus* alone is the rising quarter; 49:1's *Desde o nascer do sol até o poente* is a different phrase (*a solis ortu usque ad occásum*).
choices.102:13: First colon long (the Latin's is long too).
choices.102:14: *Recordátus est → Lembrou-se de que*. *pulvis → pó* (row). *efflorébit → florescerá*; the prefix of ἐξανθήσει is not rendered separately (*desabrochar* would lose the root of *flos*).
choices.102:16: *ámplius non → já não*, as 38:14. *cognóscet → conhecerá* (with an object, the row). *subsístet → subsistirá* (MS1932). No subject supplied for *subsistirá*: the man or the flower, as the Latin.
choices.102:17: *ab ætérno … usque in ætérnum → desde sempre … para todo o sempre* — D37 for *usque in ætérnum* (the row names 102:17), and *desde sempre* for the first member as 40:14 *a sǽculo* (D41). *autem → Mas*. Copula supplied (*é*).
choices.102:17b: *justítia → justiça*; *filii filiórum → os filhos dos filhos* (MS1932). The verse ends with a colon, as the Latin.
choices.102:18: *mémores sunt → se lembram* (memor esse row). *mandáta → mandamentos* (D15). v2: *E se lembram* was heard by the ambiguity reader as 'and if they remember' (conditional *se*); enclisis *E lembram-se* cannot be. *E que se lembram* (a relative continuing 102:17b) is the alternative the Latin's main clause does not ask for.
choices.102:19: *sedes → trono* (row, which names 102:19); *paráre → preparar* (row). The Latin's order *in cælo parávit* kept with the place before the object.
choices.102:20: *ángelus → anjo*, lowercase (row); *todos os seus anjos* as 96:7b. The participles addressed to the angels become *que* + second person plural (plural addressee, *vós*). Second colon long, as the Latin's.
choices.102:22: *ómnia ópera ejus → todas as suas obras* (row). *in omni loco → em todo lugar* (every place; *em todo o lugar* is 'in the whole place'). *dominátio → domínio*. The last words repeat 102:1a.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps102.md (no DM1962 section for this psalm) and the glossary. Rows applied: benedícere (man → God, dative), ánima mea, retribútio, oblivísci, propitiári (the row's proposal for 102:3, flagged), sanáre, infírmus, redímere, intéritus, coronáre, miseratiónes, replére, juventude (42:4), judícium (D15), notum fácere, Móyses, miserátor et miséricors (85:15), pátiens (via μακρόθυμος), irásci (84:6's copula future), in ætérnum (D23), usque in ætérnum (D37), a sǽculo (D41), fácere cum, retribúere, altitúdo, miseréri, cognóscere, pulvis, fænum (the split), serváre, testaméntum, memor esse, mandáta, sedes, paráre, dominári, ángelus, virtus (vigor for ἰσχύς), verbum/sermo (D15), Dóminus virtútum (D43), fácere voluntátem (39:9), ópera. Hard readings: 102:3 *propitiátur* (awaiting Gustavo), 102:9 *in perpétuum* beside *in ætérnum*, 102:13 *figméntum*, 102:14 the hanging *homo*, 102:16 *spíritus*, 102:20 *verbum / sermónum*.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 102:3 rhyme inside the verse (*iniquidades / enfermidades*) — the Latin has the same echo (*iniquitátibus / infirmitátes*). Length flags are mostly the counter's lack of elision (102:12 *Quanto dista‿o‿oriente do‿ocidente* is ~12 said; 102:5b, 102:9a likewise); 102:8 +4 / +4 (Portuguese *compassivo, misericordioso, paciente* against Latin trisyllables; the row's words); 102:14b +6 (the Latin's colon is long already, and elisions *como‿a‿erva*, *são‿os* bring it near); 102:4b and 102:14a −4 (Latin polysyllables against *compaixões*, *pó*); 102:17b +4 (*observam a sua aliança*, the rows' words). 102:11 takes a comma before the mediant: the Latin's colon would cut the correlative from its main verb.
